newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Timor bishop says never invited to meet Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Timor bishop says never invited to meet Kohl.

text.p: East Timor's Nobel Prize winning Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo said on Tuesday he had never been officially invited to meet German Chancellor Helmut Kohl despite claims he had rejected such an opportunity.
Belo said, however, he would have been too busy to come to Jakarta to meet Kohl anyway, even if the invitation had arrived.
"There has not been any official invitation, this matter is not so clear," Belo told Reuters by telephone from his residence in the East Timor capital of Dili.
"I have not yet received an invitation either written or verbal," Belo said.
Belo said that he had many pastoral duties in East Timor and would have been too busy to come anyway.
"I had a visit to the districts to officiate monuments and religious duties in Baucau. I could not meet him because these had been long planned," he said.
Kohl met Suharto on Monday and had talks that touched on human rights and the troubled territory of East Timor.
The German leader said he had hoped to meet Belo, adding that arrangements had been under way for about a month.
"I regret it was cancelled," Kohl told a news conference on Monday, adding that apparently Belo was busy touring East Timor.

Kohl arrived in Jakarta on Saturday for his fourth visit to Indonesia since 1983. He spent a relaxed day fishing in the Java Sea with Indonesian President Suharto on Sunday before the official leg of his visit on Monday.
He was flying to the Philippines on Tuesday morning on the second leg of an Asian tour that will also take him to Japan.
German delegation sources said Kohl had expected to meet Belo, but the bishop failed to appear at a meeting the chancellor had on Monday with other Indonesian church leaders.
Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas told a news briefing on Monday that Belo might have had previous commitments.
"I heard that Bishop Belo had some other commitments and unfortunately that (meeting) has not taken place yet. Maybe it will take place before he (Kohl) leaves but I don't know."

Belo was jointly awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize early this month together with self-exiled East Timorese resistance leader Jose Ramos-Horta, who had called on Kohl to raise the East Timor issue with Suharto.
Indonesian troops invaded East Timor in December 1975 and Jakarta declared it Indonesia's 27th province the following year in a move the United Nations has refused to recognise.
